transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-27 14:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood SE), Sasha Rivera (Helix VP Eng), Derek Cho (Helix Procurement), Anita Gomez (Helix Head of Security)

Summary (auto): Pre-procurement preflight to align legal commercial asks: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, pricing commitment structure, KMS/HSM and SSO requirements, SOC2 evidence. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines and pricing; Helix to provide SOC2 and control list; PoC kickoff week of 6/9 if approvals align.

00:00 Jordan: okay, thanks everyone for joining on time. um quick roll call, and then I want to make sure we hit the MSA/DPA items and the pricing path so procurement has what they need.
00:14 Sasha: yeah thanks Jordan. quick note we only have about 50 minutes. we wanted to double check timeline — procurement target is EOM june for vendor sign off if security is green.
00:23 Jordan: got it, that aligns with the schedule we suggested. Arjun will walk a tiny bit through deployment options but mostly legal/commercial.
00:30 Arjun: hi everyone. i'm the SE, i'll talk infra briefly, but head's up some of my details may be slightly off in terms of your internal names.
00:38 Derek: cool. top question from procurement — are we going to be licensed as hosted API or a dedicated reserved capacity? because that changes billing and SSO/KMS handling.
00:50 Jordan: great question. Redwood supports three modes: hosted API for the fastest path; dedicated for reserved GPU pools with SLA; and private/VPC for on-prem like installs. for sales path, most teams start hosted for quick prod, then move to dedicated when they need predictable throughput.
01:05 Sasha: for Helix, data residency and keys are the blockers. we need to ensure customer-managed keys and audit logs, and ideally the log retention aligns to our retention policy.
01:15 Anita: and to add, we have to see proof of SOC2 Type II and ability to do audit logs to our SIEM. also KMS must integrate with our HSM, we cannot have provider-managed plaintext keys for sensitive PII.
01:29 Jordan: understood. on the KMS point, we have KMS integrations — KMS/HSM support for Dedicated and Private deployments. hosted can support customer-managed keys via our bring-your-own-KMS approach but there are caveats on hosted key escrow. i'll mark to send specifics.
01:44 Arjun: just to flag, private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control of network and keying, but it is a heavier integration and comes with licensing commitments. dedicated allows customer-managed keys via an HSM gateway in the region typically.
01:58 Derek: procurement workflows — we need to know if Redwood requires a purchase order or if net-30 invoicing is available and whether pricing is per-token or committed capacity with overage.
02:10 Jordan: we support both. hosted tends to be usage-per-token; dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity fee plus a lower per-token delta for overage. we can do net-30 invoicing, usually enterprise customers go through a contract with monthly invoices. i'll share a pricing appendix.
02:25 Sasha: what about SLA? we're aiming for 99.9 p99 latency for our inference path, is that realistic?
02:34 Arjun: depends on model and sequence length. for smaller models and tuned batching, p95 under 200ms is achievable on dedicated. p99 99.9 is tougher and depends on pre-warm, autoscaling and KV cache hit rates. we can include a performance appendix with measured p95/p99 for sample workloads.
02:51 Anita: is there a fallback policy if capacity is exceeded? we need graceful degradation rather than silent failures.
02:58 Jordan: yes — policy-driven fallbacks. Redwood routes to compatible model variants or to a lower-cost capacity tier with explicit per-call routing; plus circuit-breaker behavior to avoid head-of-line blocking. we'll capture that in the SLA addendum.
03:10 Derek: redlines — we have standard DPA edits around data use, data deletion at rest and in transit, and liability caps. how flexible are you on caps and indemnity?
03:22 Jordan: typical ask. we can negotiate caps in enterprise tier; for smaller contracts we have a standard liability cap tied to fees. indemnity is something our legal team will review; i'll include a commercial redline template.
03:33 Sasha: on data deletion: can Redwood guarantee on-disk deletion of user content and async backups?
03:40 Arjun: yes for dedicated and private we can guarantee deletion flows and to purge KV caches and object stores; hosted deletion has propagation windows — we'll be explicit in the DPA with TTLs and retention windows.
03:53 Anita: and please clarify how long logs are stored and whether we support log forwarding to our SIEM — if logs contain sensitive metadata we can't accept long retention on Redwood's side.
04:05 Jordan: we support log forwarding and configurable retention in the console. we can add an export hook to push logs to your S3 or SIEM via secure transfer. that's in the observability addendum.
04:18 Derek: procurement needs to know SLA credits and service credits calculation. how do you compute downtime on inference endpoints?
04:26 Jordan: standard approach is measured uptime on route-level availability over a calendar month and credits scale with downtime. i'll include a sample SLA clause that maps to p99 availability over monthly windows.
04:36 Sasha: can we have an escrow for model artifacts or access controls so nobody can spin up our models outside the tenancy?
04:44 Arjun: we do tenancy isolation and model pinning. for private deployments you own the model artifacts. for hosted/dedicated we offer model version pinning and audit logs so you can see who invoked what.
04:57 Anita: we also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC mapping to our IdP groups. is that standard?
05:04 Jordan: yes SSO via SAML/SCIM and role-based access controls are supported on enterprise plans. I'll include a mapping doc.
05:13 Derek: about pricing: procurement prefers a committed tier with a right to true-up quarterly rather than unpredictable per-token bills. is quarterly true-up supported?
05:22 Jordan: yes, dedicated reserved capacity with quarterly true-ups is common. we can also structure a pilot discount for the first three months to reduce risk.
05:30 Sasha: any mention of export controls or cross-border data transfer we should note? some of our customers are EU-first and require EU-only processing.
05:39 Arjun: Redwood can pin region processing — we have EU regions and private deployments in EU for data residency. DPA will include subprocessor list and where data may transit.
05:48 Derek: procurement asks about renewal terms — auto-renew vs opt-in? and termination with cause windows?
05:56 Jordan: we typically propose 12-month agreements with auto-renew and a 60-day notice for termination; we can make that negotiable. termination for cause windows will be in the MSA.
06:05 Anita: security vetting — besides SOC2, can we do a security questionnaire (or for high-risk pieces an on-site audit)?
06:14 Jordan: absolutely, we can hand over an initial security questionnaire and schedule SOC2 artifacts. on-site audits are usually part of private engagements, but we can discuss.
06:23 Sasha: procurement also asked for a sample PoC statement of work so they can sign off internal budget. can you provide one?
06:30 Jordan: yes, we'll provide a PoC SOW that outlines scope: dedicated pool, KPI targets, duration 6 weeks, success criteria (latency, accuracy thresholds, cost per inference), and acceptance tests.
06:40 Derek: billing detail: is tax and VAT handling on Redwood side or is it on the customer?
06:47 Jordan: we can invoice with or without VAT depending on region; we'll align with your procurement team on required invoicing details.
06:54 Anita: i want to call out key rotation and split-key options. We cannot have a single exportable key. do you support HSM-backed split-key or customer HSMs?
07:04 Arjun: for private and dedicated we support HSM-backed keys and gateways; split-key patterns can be implemented as part of the integration with your HSM vendor. hosted can support BYOK with limited key usage. we'll get details in the KMS appendix.
07:18 Sasha: are there any standard exceptions Redwood asks for in the DPA (e.g., telemetry for quality improvement)?
07:26 Jordan: usually we ask for the right to use non-identifying telemetry to improve quality, but for enterprise we can make that opt-out or restrict to aggregated telemetry. that'll be in the DPA redline.
07:37 Derek: on liability and indemnity, we need a clear reciprocal indemnity for IP claims for model outputs. does Redwood accept that?
07:46 Jordan: model output IP is nuanced. by default customers retain ownership of prompts and outputs; we'll include a clause in the MSA that covers IP indemnities with mutually agreed boundaries. legal will propose wording.
07:56 Anita: can we get retention windows as a table in the DPA so compliance can review quickly?
08:03 Jordan: yes, we'll include a retention matrix (logs, transcripts, models, KV cache) with deletion timelines.
08:10 Sasha: one more—are backups encrypted at rest and who has access to keys?
08:16 Arjun: yes encrypted at rest. for dedicated/private customer-managed keys mean only you control access. hosted default keys are provider-managed unless BYOK.
08:25 Derek: procurement wants a simple deliverable list to attach to the SOW. can Redwood provide a vendor acceptance checklist?
08:33 Jordan: yes we'll provide a vendor acceptance checklist and onboarding runbook.
08:38 Sasha: okay, can we shift for a moment—what's a realistic pilot size? like qps and token volume?
08:45 Arjun: for an environment like Helix's search assistant, I'd start with a small dedicated pool (one to two GPU nodes) with autoscale for spikes; expected initial throughput 50–200 qps depending on prompt length, and cost estimates I'll put in the pricing appendix.
08:59 Derek: and what if during pilot we exceed budget — is there throttling or alerts?
09:06 Jordan: yes we can set billing alerts and hard caps to prevent runaway cost; also can provide pre-approval thresholds.
09:12 Anita: technical question — do you support prefix/KV cache isolation per customer so there's no cross-tenant leakage?
09:19 Arjun: yes, KV cache is tenant-isolated. we do continuous caching and we can purge per-tenant keys on demand. we'll also include audit trails for cache purges.
09:31 Sasha: okay we're getting to the last 10 minutes; let's summarize key commercial asks that block procurement.
09:38 Derek: 1) MSA/DPA redlines and explicit retention matrix; 2) pricing appendix for dedicated committed tier with quarterly true-up; 3) invoicing and PO vs net-30 confirmation; 4) SLA with p99 availability and fallback behavior; 5) KMS/HSM integration details and SSO mapping.
09:55 Jordan: perfect. we'll deliver: MSA/DPA redlines, PoC SOW, pricing appendix, performance appendix, KMS/SAML integration notes, and vendor acceptance checklist. target dates in next steps.
10:08 Sasha: will legal at Helix be available to review redlines quickly? we can aim for a 5 business day turn.
10:15 Derek: procurement will prioritize if we have the PoC SOW.
10:19 Anita: security will vet SOC2 and the KMS appendix. also we'll run the security questionnaire in parallel.
10:26 Jordan: next steps recap — Redwood sends documents by 2025-06-03; Helix returns SOC2 and controls by 2025-06-05; schedule PoC kickoff week of 6/9.
10:37 Sasha: sounds good. thanks everyone.
10:40 Jordan: thanks all. ACTION: Jordan/Arjun will push redlines and appendices; Derek/Anita/Sasha will circulate procurement and security artifacts.

End of meeting.
